subject: Order Form: maintenance exclusion lane & SLA triage
messages:
From: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@tidewater.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Procurements <procurements@tidewater.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Dec 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tidewater order form redlines — maintenance exclusions / credits

Hi Lauren and team,

Thanks for sending the draft order form this morning. Legal ran a pass and flagged two items we need to clarify before procurement can sign:

1) Maintenance exclusion lane — Tidewater needs clearer definitions for what counts as an excluded maintenance event (routine vs. security hotfix vs. emergent infra work). The current language is broad and could be interpreted to exclude customer-impacting events.

2) Credit computation — We need an example calculation for partial-hour downtime and how credits pro-rate when planned maintenance overlaps an outage window.

I attached our redlines (OrderForm_Tidewater_v3.pdf) and a short table with suggested uptime buckets. Could we set up a quick triage with legal + sales ops? Ideally a 30-minute slot early next week.

Thanks,
Brian
Brian Lowe
Head of Procurement — Tidewater Analytics

Subject: Re: Tidewater order form redlines — maintenance exclusions / credits

Hi Brian — appreciate the thorough pass.

Quick answers up front:
- We can carve a two-tier maintenance exclusion lane: (A) routine/planned maintenance (published windows, 48-hour notice) and (B) emergent security fixes (short-notice, higher priority). Both are counted differently for credits.
- For partial-hour downtime we propose prorating credits to the minute with a floor of one minute; we'll provide the math and a worked example.

Action plan: Jordan, can you bring the proposed credit table and the exact replacement language for section 3.2 (Planned Maintenance & Exclusions)? Kimberly, could you confirm whether the emergent security exclusion needs additional guardrails to avoid overbroad interpretation from a legal perspective?

Brian — I'm attaching our draft SLA rollforward table (SLA_Rollforward_Table.xlsx) with the proposed parity language. Would next Tuesday 10:00 AM PT work for 30 minutes? If not, suggest two alternatives.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 03 Dec 2028 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tidewater order form redlines — maintenance exclusions / credits

Lauren — thanks, attaching my proposed language (pasted below) and the revised uptime buckets.

Proposed excerpt for Order Form (suggested insertion into Section 3.2):
"Planned Maintenance" means maintenance events scheduled at least 48 hours in advance and communicated via the Customer Console. "Emergent Security Maintenance" means maintenance required to mitigate a verified security vulnerability; Redwood will provide as much notice as feasible and document the root cause. Planned Maintenance will not be considered Unavailability for credit calculations provided it falls within the published maintenance window. Emergent Security Maintenance will be excluded from availability calculations only where Redwood demonstrates the action was necessary to remediate an active security threat.

Uptime buckets (sample):
- >= 99.95% — no credits
- 99.5%–99.95% — 5% monthly credit
- 99.0%–99.49% — 15% monthly credit
- < 99.0% — 30% monthly credit

Credit calc note: credits pro-rate to the minute when an incident overlaps a planned maintenance window. We also propose an example calculation appended to the order form to avoid ambiguity.

Kimberly — can you confirm the emergent security language isn't exposing us to broad interpretation? If so, suggest edits here and I will fold into the redline to send back to Tidewater.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@tidewater.com>

Lauren / Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposed text. The emergent security carve-out language looks reasonable to our counsel provided we add a requirement that Redwood publish a post-action report within 7 business days for any event excluded under that clause (root cause + mitigation steps).

The uptime buckets and prorating approach are acceptable; procurement will want the worked example attached directly into the PDF we sign. Can you produce a single consolidated redline (PDF) that includes the example calculation and the emergent security reporting commitment? Once we have that, I can route to my GC for a final quick sign-off and push to DocuSign.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to deliver consolidated redline PDF + example calculation and confirm the 7-business-day post-action report commitment in writing.
- Tidewater legal to confirm by end of week and, if approved, procurement will send signature request.

If you prefer, we can take the remaining confirmation offline with Kimberly.

Appreciate it —
Brian
